rationale: This computable general equilibrium simulation models future water availability, agricultural productivity shocks, environmental flow reserves and macroeconomic real income/welfare across Mediterranean economies. It does not examine household or community domestic water or sanitation service access (E07) and relies on macroeconomic scenario simulation rather than empirical evidence on WASH access.
plain_vs_narrow_note: Excluded under both narrow and plain readings of Criterion 2 because the study fails Criterion 1 (focuses on agricultural water productivity and ambient environmental flows rather than household/community water or sanitation service access), Criterion 3 (computable general equilibrium simulation exercise rather than empirical primary research or systematic synthesis) and Criterion 4 (macroeconomic income and welfare outcomes rather than domestic WASH access).

evidence_quotes.quote: System-Wide Implications of Changing Water Availability and Agricultural Productivity in the Mediterranean Economies
This includes an assessment of future water availability and a general equilibrium macroeconomic analysis of changes in agricultural productivity.
We find evidence of a dramatic cut in the supply of water for agriculture in the Middle East.
